profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, also known as Stanford HAI, is a nonprofit university lab founded in 2019 and based in Stanford, CA, USA. Its site states that its mission is to advance humanity through AI and data science, with work focused on discovery, technological innovation, educational transformation, and societal impact. The institute describes human-centered AI as an approach that prioritizes human needs, values, and well-being throughout the development and deployment of AI systems. It runs fellowship and grant programs, affinity groups for students, and training programs for business leaders, policymakers and civil servants, and K-12 educators. Fei-Fei Li is named as Founding Director and Senior Fellow, and James Landay as Denning Director.

Among its programs is the AI Index, whose 2026 Annual Report is described as the ninth edition, published April 2026 by the AI Index Steering Committee at Stanford HAI under DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2606.15708 and licensed CC BY-ND 4.0. The AI Index programme page also covers the Global AI Vibrancy tool. The site highlights research on benchmarks, on emergent agent behavior and independent evaluation, and on AI privacy, and notes that over 6,000 of the world's 7,000-plus living languages remain digitally disadvantaged. Named contributors include Surya Ganguli, Diyi Yang, Rob Reich, Jennifer King, Caroline Meinhardt, Thomas Mullaney, and Juan N. Pava.

The institute's recorded aliases include Stanford HAI, Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, HAI, and AI Index. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for it. Its recorded law exposure is in California, with a count of 281.
